products.name: Apple HomePod mini 2
products.badge: Cheapest way to get a HomeKit home hub
products.summary: A small plug-in smart speaker that doubles as a HomeKit home hub, so automations and remote control work when you are away. Apple lists Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 6, Thread networking, a temperature and humidity sensor and a 20W power adapter in the box.
products.renterNote: Suits an iPhone-owning renter starting HomeKit who wants a hub that sits on a shelf with no drilling. Caveat: it needs an iPhone or iPad to set up, and Apple's current spec page lists HomePod mini 2, so older first-generation units that guides describe may differ.
pros: Acts as a HomeKit home hub for remote access and automations, per the guides read
Plugs into a wall outlet; nothing to mount or drill
Thread networking and a built-in temperature and humidity sensor, per Apple
cons: Requires an iPhone or iPad running current iOS to set up
Hub role only helps Apple Home devices; it does not control Alexa-only devices

products.name: Apple TV 4K (4th generation)
products.badge: Best hub if you also want a streaming box
products.summary: A TV streaming box that also serves as a HomeKit home hub. Apple lists a 128GB model with A19 chip, Wi-Fi 7, Gigabit Ethernet, Bluetooth 6 and Thread networking technology.
products.renterNote: Suits a renter who already wants an Apple streaming box and wants it to double as an always-on hub. Caveat: it needs a TV with HDMI and an HDMI cable (sold separately), and it stays at the TV rather than moving around the home like a speaker.
pros: Doubles as a HomeKit home hub and has Thread, per Apple and the guides read
Wired Gigabit Ethernet option for a steadier hub connection
Sits on a shelf; nothing to mount
cons: Needs an HDMI TV and an HDMI cable sold separately
More than a hub-only buyer needs if they do not stream
